channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Bedrock Data Launches Intent-Aware AI Agent DLP
item.description: Bedrock Data launched Agent DLP, a runtime data loss prevention tool that infers user intent and evaluates AI agent actions against policy. The tool weighs intent and behavior, enabling continued AI agent use while protecting sensitive data across tool and LLM calls. It also supports off-the-shelf integrations and offers a policy enforcement framework for AI workflows.

item.title: Elastic Deploys AI Agents to Triage SOC Alerts
item.description: Elastic Security 9.6 introduces AlertZero, AI agents that triage alerts, hunt threats, and tune detection rules. The release adds Linux ransomware protection, expands entity resolution, and adds 143 detection rules for AI agents and LLM platforms. AlertZero groups workers into four watches-triage, threat hunting, detection engineering, and others-to automate SOC backlog.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Thunderbird Update for Important Vulnerabilities
item.description: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.6 receives a security update for Thunderbird, addressing several important vulnerabilities. The advisory references multiple CVEs with CVSS base scores, indicating potential remote code execution or privilege escalation if unpatched. Users should apply the update immediately to mitigate the risk, as the patch resolves all identified flaws.

item.title: RHEL 10 cifs-utils Update Released
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for cifs-utils on RHEL 10, fixing vulnerabilities that could enable remote code execution via SMB. Each flaw carries a CVSS base score, but the advisory lists no specific CVE identifiers. Apply the patch through standard RHEL update channels immediately; no configuration changes are required.

item.title: Infrastructure Vulnerabilities Highlight Systemic Fragility
item.description: Schneier's essay examines how America’s critical infrastructure remains fragile due to aging systems, piecemeal patching, and hobbyist maintenance. The author argues that centralization and incremental upgrades create a single point of failure, causing widespread outages when components fail. The piece calls for systemic investment and coordinated security practices to reduce the risk of cascading infrastructure breakdowns.

item.title: Azure API Management flaw used to steal credentials
item.description: Microsoft warned that a vulnerability in Azure API Management (APIM) was exploited to exfiltrate credentials from customers’ instances, affecting Norwegian energy firms and others. The flaw in APIM Classic tiers lets attackers bypass authentication and retrieve stored secrets, potentially compromising downstream services. Microsoft recommends applying the latest APIM patch, disabling Classic tiers, and rotating exposed credentials immediately.

item.title: KEPCO Data Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Personal Records
item.description: Hackers accessed KEPCO’s customer portal and supplier relationship management platform, exfiltrating personal data of approximately 1.5 million users. The breach involved names, contact details, and possibly financial identifiers, though the full data scope is unclear. KEPCO has not yet released a detailed incident response plan; affected parties should monitor for identity theft and consider credit monitoring services.

item.title: EvilTokens Phishing Persists After Microsoft Takedown
item.description: Despite Microsoft shutting down the EvilTokens phishing-as-a-service kit, attackers continue to deploy new phishing hosts targeting Microsoft 365 accounts. The campaign exploits social engineering to trick users into revealing credentials, potentially granting attackers full access to corporate Microsoft 365 environments. Security teams should enforce multi-factor authentication, monitor for anomalous sign-ins, and educate users about phishing indicators.

item.title: LibreOffice Vulnerabilities Patched in RHEL 9.4 SAP
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for LibreOffice on RHEL 9.4 Update Services for SAP Solutions, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update carries an Important impact rating, with CVSS base scores available via CVE references, but no active exploitation has been reported. Administrators should apply the latest LibreOffice package to mitigate the identified risks.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical Update for ruby:4.0
item.description: A critical flaw in the ruby:4.0 module for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 triggered an urgent security update. The vulnerability, rated with a high CVSS score, permits remote code execution via the Ruby interpreter and is linked to several CVEs. Red Hat released the patch in RHSA-2026-102883; users must apply it immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat Releases cifs-utils Patch for RHEL 9.8
item.description: Red Hat issued a cifs-utils update for RHEL 9.8 EUS, fixing vulnerabilities that could enable remote code execution via SMB. Each flaw is linked to a CVE and carries a CVSS base score, with Red Hat rating the issue as Important. Apply the patch or upgrade to the latest RHEL 9.8 release to eliminate the risk.

item.title: MFA Bypassed via Phone Scams Targeting Microsoft 365
item.description: Cybercriminals posing as corporate IT support trick employees into revealing Microsoft 365 credentials, bypassing MFA to access OneDrive and SharePoint. They exfiltrated emails and files from compromised accounts and demanded ransom via Teams or email, exploiting social engineering. Teams should enforce verification protocols, monitor anomalous activity, and restrict external sharing to mitigate similar attacks.

item.title: Microsoft Patches Azure API Management Flaw Targeting Secrets
item.description: Microsoft discovered a flaw in Azure API Management Classic that allowed attackers to search for access tokens and secrets. The vulnerability, enabling credential theft and unauthorized API access, was reported by Norway's National Security Authority and is actively exploited. Microsoft released a patch in the latest update; customers should apply it immediately and audit API permissions to mitigate risk.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102514: Important: buildah, conmon, container-selinux, containers-common, criu, fuse-overlayfs, gvisor-tap-vsock, oci-seccomp-bpf-hook, podman, skopeo, and slirp4netns security, bug fix, and enhancement update
item.description: An update for buildah, conmon, container-selinux, containers-common, criu, fuse-overlayfs, gvisor-tap-vsock, oci-seccomp-bpf-hook, podman, skopeo, and slirp4netns is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.

item.title: Elecbrakes Bluetooth Flaws Enable Forced Trailer Braking
item.description: Critical Bluetooth vulnerabilities in Elecbrakes trailer controllers allow nearby attackers to force braking, potentially causing accidents. The flaw exploits insecure Bluetooth pairing and command authentication, enabling remote manipulation of braking systems without user interaction. Manufacturers should update firmware to patch the vulnerabilities and disable unused Bluetooth interfaces to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat Issues container-tools:rhel8 Security Update for RHEL 8.4
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the container-tools:rhel8 module on RHEL 8.4 AMCS and EUS LLA, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update contains fixes for issues with CVSS scores listed in the CVE references, but no active exploitation has been reported. Red Hat recommends applying the patch through the standard RHEL update channels to mitigate potential remote code execution.

item.title: Peninsula Energy Halts Trading After Mine Cyber Incident
item.description: Peninsula Energy reported a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming uranium project, temporarily disrupting operations and prompting a trading halt. The breach details remain undisclosed, but the company indicated that critical operational systems were impacted, raising concerns over supply chain continuity. Peninsula Energy is coordinating with cybersecurity teams and regulators to assess the incident and resume trading.

item.title: CISA Flags Exploited VMware, SAP, Cisco, Apache Flaws
item.description: CISA added four exploited vulnerabilities affecting VMware vCenter, SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway, and Apache Roller to its KEV catalog. All four flaws were actively exploited in the wild, prompting CISA to urge federal civilian agencies to patch by November 23. Administrators should apply vendor patches or workarounds immediately to mitigate the exploitation risk.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102880: Important: ImageMagick security update
item.description: An update for ImageMagick is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 Extended Lifecycle Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: GlobeTopper faces up to $2.5 million in lost revenue after hackers steal $70,000 in gift cards
item.description: According to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), parent company iQSTEL said GlobeTopper detected the intrusion on October 22 and took the platform offline the next morning after spotting further unauthorized activity.

item.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship for GitHub PR Review
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Ship in beta, letting Claude Code review GitHub pull requests, push fixes, and approve changes when policy allows. The tool does not merge code automatically; repository permissions and branch rules still govern integration. Security teams can use Claude Ship to automate reviews, but must enforce branch protection and review policies to retain control.

item.title: Windows Remote Access API Vulnerability Enables SYSTEM Privilege Escalation
item.description: A flaw in the Windows Remote Access API lets an attacker with limited local access run code with SYSTEM privileges. Microsoft assigned CVE-2026-119853 a CVSS score of 7.8 and rated the issue Important, but no active exploitation has been reported. Microsoft released a patch on Patch Tuesday; teams should apply it immediately via Windows Update or WSUS.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102854: Critical: ruby security update
item.description: An update for ruby is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Critical. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship for AI Code Review
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Ship, a beta AI suite that reviews pull requests, fixes issues, and approves changes per team policies. It merges code review, automated fixes, and policy enforcement to speed development while preserving quality. Deploying Claude Ship into CI/CD pipelines lets teams set approval thresholds and monitor false positives for safe integration.

item.title: NVIDIA Kernel Vulnerability Enables Hypervisor Out-of-Bounds
item.description: A local attacker with hypervisor access can exploit a missing Reverse Map Table check during IOMMU buffer access, enabling an out-of-bounds condition that may corrupt SEV-SNP guest memory. The flaw, CVE-2023-20585, is a local privilege escalation that could undermine guest isolation, with no public exploit yet. Ubuntu released kernel patches; administrators should update or backport the fix.

item.title: Ubuntu Releases Kernel Patch for Multiple Azure Vulnerabilities
item.description: Ubuntu released a kernel update that patches multiple Azure vulnerabilities across subsystems such as ARM64, S390, x86, Bluetooth, GPU, and network drivers. The flaws allow remote or local privilege escalation, enabling attackers to compromise system integrity and run arbitrary code on virtual machines. Admins should promptly apply the latest kernel update or backport the patches to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Kernel Vulnerabilities Threaten System Integrity
item.description: A range of kernel subsystems in Linux contain vulnerabilities that could enable attackers to compromise system integrity. The flaws affect architecture layers, device drivers, and file system components, posing a broad local privilege escalation risk. Ubuntu released kernel patches addressing these issues; administrators should update to the latest kernel or backport the fixes.

item.title: Ubuntu and Red Hat Patch NVIDIA Kernel Vulnerabilities
item.description: Ubuntu and Red Hat have released kernel updates to address multiple NVIDIA subsystem vulnerabilities affecting Linux systems. The flaws span device drivers, data paths, architecture modules, cryptographic APIs, and hardware interfaces, potentially enabling privilege escalation or data exfiltration. Administrators should apply the latest kernel patches immediately to mitigate risk, as no active exploitation has been reported.

item.title: Linux Kernel Vulnerabilities Patched
item.description: Multiple kernel vulnerabilities were identified across various subsystems, potentially allowing attackers to compromise affected Linux systems. The flaws affect stream parsing, architecture modules, drivers, Bluetooth, GPU, Hyper-V, network, and other hardware interfaces, yet no active exploitation has been reported. Red Hat and Ubuntu have issued kernel updates that patch these subsystems; administrators should install the latest kernel to mitigate risk.

item.title: Linux Kernel Vulnerabilities Patching Update Released
item.description: The Linux kernel contains multiple vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-99218, that could allow attackers to compromise affected systems. These flaws span cryptographic API, file system infrastructure, key management, io_uring, PID namespace, and tracing subsystems, potentially enabling privilege escalation or arbitrary code execution. Kernel maintainers have released an update patching all listed CVEs; administrators should apply the update promptly.

item.title: Microsoft Uncovers Linux Kernel Vulnerabilities in Azure
item.description: Microsoft identified multiple Linux kernel flaws in Azure that could allow attackers to compromise affected systems. The vulnerabilities affect IPv4 networking, Ethernet bridge, Netfilter, SCTP, and XFRM subsystems, and are catalogued as CVE-2026-64564, CVE-2026-98432, and CVE-2026-99999, potentially enabling remote code execution. Administrators should apply the latest kernel updates or install the provided patches to eliminate the exploitation vector.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot CVE-2026-50691 Enables Privilege Escalation
item.description: Microsoft disclosed CVE-2026-50691, a critical flaw in Microsoft 365 Copilot that lets a low-privileged user elevate network permissions without user interaction. Scored 9.9 on CVSS 3.1, the bug exploits a logic error in Copilot’s permission model, enabling unauthorized access to protected resources. Microsoft urges customers to apply the November 19 patch via Microsoft Update or by updating the Copilot add-in.

item.title: Red Hat Issues python3.12 Security Update for RHEL 9.6
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for python3.12 on RHEL 9.6 EUS, addressing code-execution vulnerabilities. The patch fixes issues with CVSS scores of 7.8-8.5, as listed in the CVE references, with no active exploitation reported. Red Hat recommends applying the update via standard RHEL channels immediately to mitigate potential remote code execution.

item.title: Red Hat Recommends Python-OAuthlib Patch for RHEL 10.2
item.description: Red Hat released an important security update for python-oauthlib on RHEL 10.2 Extended Update Support, targeting authentication library flaws. The update fixes multiple high-severity bugs that could allow credential misuse or unauthorized token issuance, though CVE identifiers are not disclosed. Apply RHSA-2026:102851 via the Customer Portal or use yum/dnf to install the latest python-oauthlib package immediately.

item.title: Red Hat Recommends PHP Update for RHEL 9.2
item.description: A critical PHP update is released for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.2 Update Services for SAP Solutions, fixing runtime vulnerabilities. The patch addresses multiple high-severity flaws that could enable remote code execution or privilege escalation, though CVE IDs are not listed. Red Hat advises applying RHSA-2026:102847 immediately via the Customer Portal or using yum/dnf to install the updated PHP package.

item.title: AI Hackers Access 3,392 Accounts, Decrypt 50 SSH Keys
item.description: An attacker employing the CyberStrikeAI framework accessed 3,392 user accounts and active session tokens during a four-day cloud intrusion at two AWS accounts and seven EKS clusters in October 2026. The operator also decrypted a bastion host database, recovering 50 SSH private keys, exposing critical credentials. Security teams should isolate affected accounts, rotate credentials, and investigate the breach.

item.title: Top Attack Path Management Tools Ranked for 2026
item.description: Cyber Security News evaluated defensive tools, ranking the top ten attack path management solutions available in 2026. These tools analyze complex attack chains by converting vulnerability lists into graphs mapping misconfigurations, excessive permissions, and credential reuse. Security teams can deploy attack path management software to identify critical choke points and remediate high-risk operational vectors efficiently.

item.title: Hackers Plant Backdoors in 6 WordPress Plugins to Steal Passwords and Take Over Websites
item.description: Hackers planted a remote-control backdoor in nine versions of six WordPress plugins from WP connect on November 22, 2026. The malware could let an attacker steal password hashes, run commands, and take over a website. But WordPress.org blocked the tainted versions before distributing them and closed all six plugins that evening.

item.title: Elecbrakes Bluetooth Flaw Enables Remote Brake Control
item.description: A critical Bluetooth flaw in Elecbrakes trailer brake controllers, CVE-2026-96805, lets attackers within range manipulate brakes without pairing. Rated 9.6 CVSS, the flaw exploits command injection in Bluetooth, enabling unauthenticated remote brake control. Manufacturers should push firmware updates disabling unsecured Bluetooth commands; users must avoid exposing controllers to untrusted devices until patched.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important Security Update for MariaDB
item.description: Red Hat released a security update addressing security flaws in the mariadb:11.8 module for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9. Red Hat Product Security rated the operational impact of these vulnerabilities as Important based on Common Vulnerability Scoring System metrics. System administrators should apply the RHSA-2026:102830 advisory updates to mitigate potential exploitation risks across enterprise RHEL environments.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important WebKit2GTK3 Update
item.description: Red Hat released an important security update for webkit2gtk3 on RHEL 9.2 for SAP Solutions. The patch addresses undisclosed vulnerabilities that could enable code execution or system compromise, with CVSS scores linked in the CVE references and mitigate potential privilege escalation. Administrators should apply the update immediately to eliminate the exploitation vector.

item.title: Hackers Compromise Check Point Management Servers
item.description: Hackers have compromised Check Point Security Management Servers, which store firewall rule sets that govern corporate traffic filtering. The ongoing campaign has affected at least 22 organizations worldwide, and attackers retain active access to many servers, exposing critical network controls. Check Point recommends applying the latest firmware patches, disabling unused management interfaces, and monitoring for anomalous configuration changes.

item.title: Google Cloud CISO Discusses Agentic AI in SOC
item.description: Google Cloud CISO Chris Betz spoke about agentic AI in security operations during a Help Net Security interview. He noted that automation lets attackers traverse networks in minutes, questioned junior analyst roles, and urged reassessment of controls and board oversight. Betz advised organizations to evolve SOC workflows with AI-driven threat hunting and governance to counter increasingly stealthy espionage groups.

item.title: Ransomware Groups Multiply Despite Fewer Victim Payments
item.description: Check Point Research’s State of Ransomware Q3 2026 report lists 2,830 victims on data-leak sites, the highest quarterly total on record. July, August, and September accounted for 964, 1,042, and 824 victims respectively, indicating a sustained expansion of active ransomware groups. The report shows declining payments but continued brand proliferation, stressing the need for stronger defensive measures.

item.title: AWS European Sovereign Cloud: Architecture and Compliance Overview
item.description: AWS European Sovereign Cloud offers infrastructure designed to meet European data sovereignty requirements, providing isolated regions and compliance with local regulations. The architecture provides physical and logical separation, encryption controls, and audit capabilities, enabling organizations to retain full data control while leveraging AWS services. Customers can evaluate the platform against certifications and compliance frameworks to determine suitability for sensitive workloads.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Cockpit Security Update
item.description: Red Hat issued an Important security update for the cockpit component on Enterprise Linux 9.4 Update Services for SAP Solutions. The advisory cites several CVEs with CVSS scores, but no specific CVE ID is listed. Administrators should apply the cockpit update immediately to mitigate the identified vulnerabilities and consult the CVE links for detailed impact.
